chapter_theme: Seeing what is really so is what ends suffering and birth: mistaking the unreal for the real starts it, and stripping off appearances ends it. The chapter never says what மெய்ப்பொருள் is, and this silence is where its commentators divide most.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar reads a sequence: confusion as the root of birth (351), true sight as the way to release (352-354), its definition (355), three means which he names hearing, reflection and contemplation (356, 357, 358), and how remaining suffering ends (359-360).

351.reading: A joyless birth comes from the confusion that perceives what isn't real as real.
351.nuance: The verse doesn't say which things are unreal. Parimelazhagar fills this in as denying rebirth, the fruit of deeds, and God, adding the stump mistaken for a man and shell for silver. Kalaignar has no birth in view, only a life that goes poorly.

positions.position: The false view is to deny rebirth, the fruit of deeds, and God.
positions.quote: அவ் விபரீத உணர்வாவது, மறுபிறப்பும், இருவினைப் பயனும், கடவுளும் இல்லை எனவும்,

352.reading: For those of stainless sight, who have left confusion behind, it removes darkness and brings joy.
352.nuance: What is the darkness? Parimelazhagar says hell, Manakkudavar and Kalaignar say ignorance, and Pope's gloss says the darkness of future births. The verse leaves it as a word.

353.reading: For those who have left doubt and become clear, the sky is nearer than the earth they stand on.
353.nuance: Doubt here is the obstacle in its own right. Parimelazhagar makes an unusually candid point: every school's texts refute the others, so which is true can only be settled through one's own experience. The image of the far as nearer than the near is very bold.

354.reading: Even having gained the five-fold awareness, there is no benefit for those who lack true perception.

positions.position: The five-fold awareness is the mind itself, gathered into concentration, and even this falls short.
It is all that can be known by the five senses.
It is having subdued the five senses.

355.reading: Whatever a thing is and of whatever nature, seeing the true thing in that thing is understanding.
355.nuance: One of the Kural's best-known definitions, and it is doctrinally open. Parimelazhagar removes a Chera king's rank, lineage, looks and names as conventions, down to the elements and beyond, while Kalaignar asks only that we not be fooled by appearances. It is both a metaphysical and a practical line.

positions.position: One discards the world's imputed conceptions and sees what remains.
positions.quote: பொருள் தோறும் உலகத்தார் கற்பித்துக் கொண்டு வழங்குகின்ற கற்பனைகளைக் கழித்து, நின்ற உண்மையைக் காண்பது

positions.position: It is about not being taken in by outward looks.

356.reading: Those who have learned here and seen the true thing will reach the path of not coming back here.
356.nuance: Here learning is an actual route to the truth, in contrast to 373. For Parimelazhagar this is hearing from an experienced teacher, the first of his three means.

positions.position: 'Not coming back' means no return to birth.
It means no return to the household life from renunciation.

357.reading: If the mind ponders and knows with certainty what is, one needn't think again of birth.
357.nuance: உள்ளது, 'what is', is the plainest of the chapter's names for the goal. This reading assumes the commentators' உணரின் over the verse text's உணரான், as noted in source_issues.

positions.position: There is no need to expect a further birth for such a person.
Those who truly investigate won't believe in rebirth at all, which reverses the claim into a denial of the doctrine.

358.reading: Understanding is seeing the perfect thing called the excellent, so that the folly called birth departs.
358.nuance: The verse calls birth itself a folly, an astonishing metaphor that all three commentators have to unpack, each differently. Pope's 'man's dignity' for சிறப்பு goes in a different direction from all of them.

positions.position: It means the ignorance that is the first cause of birth.
The folly is thinking that oneself is born and dies, when one's real standing has neither.
positions.quote: தான் பிறந்தானாக வும் செத்தானாகவும் கருதுகின்ற அறியாமையை விட்டுத்,

positions.position: The ignorance is the very belief in a next birth.

359.reading: If one knows the support and lives so that supports perish, the pains due to cling won't destroy that life and cling.
359.nuance: One word, சார்பு, does double service. Parimelazhagar adds that the fruit even of good deeds counts as 'pain' here, because it causes birth, which is a hard saying.

positions.position: The support to be known is the supreme reality on which all rests, and the supports to end are the attachments.
The support is what attaches to oneself, the dependence on deeds.
It simply means finding out the causes of one's troubles and letting go of them.

360.reading: When even the names of the three, desire, anger and confusion, perish, pain perishes.
360.nuance: நாமம், 'the name', is what must go, so they aren't merely suppressed. This triad resembles the three poisons in Buddhist teaching, a comparison that is mine and no commentator's. Parimelazhagar derives it by reducing a Sanskrit list of five faults.

positions.position: The Sanskrit list of five faults reduces to these three, since ego falls under ignorance and craving under desire.
positions.quote: இவர் அவற்றுள் அகங்காரம் அவிச்சைக்கண்ணும் அவாவுதல் ஆசைக்கண்ணும் அடங்குதலான், 'மூன்று' என்றார்.

links.note: Their second lines are identical. 423 applies it to what we are told: whoever says it, find the truth in it. 355 applies it to what things are: whatever their appearance, find the truth in them. The same habit of mind is both critical thinking and metaphysics.

343 demands crushing the domain of the five senses. 354, on Kalaignar's reading, says that this gets you nothing without true perception. The disciplined renouncer of chapter 35 isn't the goal in itself.

For Parimelazhagar, the schools conflict on everything in 242 and yet converge on அருள். On 353, he says that their conflict leaves doubt only experience can settle. Together they give his view of religious pluralism: agreement in ethics, and no resolution by argument in metaphysics.
356 makes learning (கற்று) the route to seeing the true thing. 373 says however much one studies, one's own understanding prevails. Chapter 38 thus undercuts the very means this one recommends.

35 defines virtue as conduct free of envy, craving, anger and harsh words. 360 lists desire, anger and confusion, whose ending ends pain. Anger and desire appear in both lists, and the shift to confusion in 360 marks the shift from conduct to knowledge.
Both describe those of மாசறு காட்சி who are free of மருள். 352 says what it does for them; 199 says what it looks like from outside: they don't utter a meaningless word even by accident.

source_issues: 357: the verse text reads உணரான், 'does not know', while Parimelazhagar's gloss, உள்ளது உணரின், and Pope and the others all read the conditional உணரின். As printed, the verse would make no sense with the commentary.
360: the verse text has the corruption இநவ்முன்றன் for இவைமூன்றன்.
351: no Manakkudavar commentary is aligned to this verse.
